topic.angle: A disaster that changed how London was built

card.title: The fire that banned wooden fronts

body.claim: After the Great Fire of 1666, London was rebuilt in brick and stone instead of wood.
body.why: The fire started in a bakery in Pudding Lane on 2 September 1666 and burned until 5 September, destroying around 13,200 to 13,500 houses and St Paul's Cathedral. The Rebuilding of London Act banned wood from the outside of buildings. The rebuild also brought wider streets and open wharves along the Thames. The traditional death toll is six, though some historians think it was higher.

probes.question: What change did London's rebuilding bring?
options: Buildings made of brick and stone, not wood
